overall_summary: Bitcoin faces clear pressure from Strategy’s fresh sales and lingering exploit fallout, while a hot ISM print has firmed the dollar and dialed back Fed-cut hopes. ETF inflows and talk of a near-term Hormuz deal provide some offset, but the balance of catalysts leans defensive for crypto. Traders will watch today’s data and any diplomacy headlines for the next swing.
key_points: Hot ISM PMI firms dollar, cools cut bets

items.title: Coldcard Exploit Losses Climb Toward $130 Million
items.summary: Galaxy Research now pegs confirmed thefts from the Coldcard hardware wallet firmware flaw at about 1,596 Bitcoin across thousands of addresses, with a suspected fourth wave that could push the total near 2,055 BTC or roughly 130 million dollars. The bug traces to weak random-number generation in firmware from 2021, and most stolen coins remain unmoved while investigators loop in law enforcement and exchanges. Traders should care because it reignites self-custody fears right as Bitcoin tries to stabilize near 64,000, potentially driving more holders toward ETFs or exchanges and adding overhead selling pressure if victims scramble.
items.impact: Short-term sentiment hit and possible defensive selling or rotation out of self-custody

items.title: Strategy Sells Another 1,638 Bitcoin for $105 Million
items.summary: Strategy, formerly MicroStrategy, disclosed selling 1,638 BTC last week for about 105 million dollars, bringing holdings down to 842,138 coins, while also issuing stock and using proceeds to boost its dollar reserve to 4 billion and repurchase preferred STRC shares. This is the company's third Bitcoin sale of 2026 as it funds dividends and stabilizes its preferreds after abandoning a pure never-sell stance. Traders should watch because the largest corporate holder adding supply undercuts the treasury accumulation narrative and can weigh on price, even if the amounts remain small relative to its stack.
items.impact: Adds spot supply and dents corporate HODL confidence

items.title: First U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Set to Close
items.summary: Hashdex will liquidate its tiny DEFI spot Bitcoin ETF after August 17, the first closure of a U.S. spot Bitcoin fund, with only 14.7 million dollars in assets versus BlackRock IBIT's tens of billions. The firm cited low AUM, liquidity, costs and waning investor interest as capital chases AI returns instead, with the broader spot ETF complex seeing multi-month net outflows. This matters for traders as a sign of product concentration and cooler institutional demand outside the biggest names, though it does not threaten the category overall.
items.impact: Highlights flow concentration and opportunity-cost pressure without killing the ETF complex

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Post $170 Million Inflow Monday
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly 170 million dollars in net inflows on August 3, led by BlackRock's IBIT, snapping recent weakness after a prior week of net outflows. Data from trackers show the daily print at about 2,680 Bitcoin equivalent, providing a modest demand bid as price rebounded toward 64,000. Traders should note this as evidence that institutional buying can still appear on dips even in a quiet August tape and extreme-fear readings, supporting the floor near current levels if it continues.
items.impact: Provides incremental spot demand and cushions downside

items.title: Bernstein Warns Clarity Act Stall Risks Crypto Selloff
items.summary: Bernstein told clients that failure to pass the CLARITY Act before the Senate's August 7 recess would likely trigger a near-term selloff in Bitcoin and crypto, calling it the most consequential market-structure bill, though the firm expects the SEC and CFTC to accelerate their own rulemaking under Project Crypto regardless. Odds have slipped and lawmakers face a tight window, with some reports of a possible vote this week. This is key for traders because regulatory clarity is a major overhang; a miss could spark risk-off while any progress or agency action could stabilize sentiment.
items.impact: Unresolved catalyst that could drive volatility either way this week

items.title: BlackRock Tokenizes Access to $311 Billion European MMFs
items.summary: BlackRock launched tokenized share classes giving on-chain access to 311 billion dollars of its European money-market funds across multiple currencies and markets, working with JPMorgan's platform, just after expanding similar U.S. tokenized cash products. The move targets corporate treasurers and asset managers seeking blockchain settlement and transfer for traditional cash vehicles. Traders should care because it advances the real-world asset and tokenization thesis led by the world's largest asset manager, reinforcing institutional infrastructure that ultimately supports crypto rails and Bitcoin adjacency.
items.impact: Positive for RWA adoption and long-term institutional crypto infrastructure

items.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI Surges to 55.6, Strongest Since 2022
items.summary: US factory activity accelerated sharply in July, with the ISM Manufacturing PMI hitting 55.6 against expectations of 54.0 and up from 53.3. Production jumped to a multi-year high, new orders stayed solid, and employment expanded for the first time in a long stretch to 52.8. Prices paid eased a bit but remained elevated near 71. Traders should care because this hot print reinforces economic resilience, lifts odds of a Fed rate hike later this year after the recent split decision, and supports the dollar while raising the bar for risk assets.
items.impact: Higher rate-hike odds and firmer dollar pressure Bitcoin and equities

items.title: Treasury Lifts Q3 Borrowing Estimate to $739 Billion
items.summary: The US Treasury raised its third-quarter privately held net marketable borrowing forecast to 739 billion dollars, 68 billion higher than the May projection, mainly due to weaker expected cash flows. Fourth-quarter borrowing is pegged at 628 billion. Auction size details come Wednesday. This matters for traders as heavier supply can push yields higher and tighten financial conditions, especially with long-end yields already elevated and inflation risks from energy still in play.
items.impact: Increased bond supply risks higher yields and tighter liquidity

items.title: Treasury Yields Drop as Oil Plunges on Iran De-escalation Hopes
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell nearly 7 basis points to around 4.68 percent on Monday, with the 2-year and 30-year also lower, tracking a sharp drop in oil prices. The move followed President Trump's comments on possible renewed talks with Iran after holding off strikes. Iranian officials pushed back on direct negotiations. Lower yields ease financial conditions and reduce rate pressure, which crypto traders watch closely for risk appetite support, though geopolitics remain fluid.
items.impact: Lower yields supportive for risk assets and Bitcoin

items.title: Construction Spending Unexpectedly Falls 0.1% in June
items.summary: US construction spending dipped 0.1 percent in June to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of about 2.17 trillion dollars, missing forecasts for a 0.2 percent rise, with residential outlays weaker. Nonresidential held up better, helped by data centers. Year-over-year spending is down over 3 percent. Soft housing-related data can temper growth concerns and influence rate expectations ahead of bigger labor reports this week.
items.impact: Mildly soft data may cap yield upside short-term

items.title: Key US Data Due Today: Trade Balance, JOLTS, Factory Orders
items.summary: Tuesday brings the June international trade balance, expected to show a narrower deficit around 73 billion dollars, June factory orders forecast near flat to plus 0.2 percent, and the closely watched JOLTS job openings report for June, seen easing to about 7.4 million from 7.59 million. These feed into Friday's employment report and Fed thinking. Crypto traders need to watch for surprises that shift rate-cut or hike probabilities and dollar moves.
items.impact: Data surprises could swing yields, dollar, and risk sentiment

items.title: Dollar Firms Near 100 as Markets Reassess Fed Path Post-ISM
items.summary: The US dollar index hovered near 100 after recovering some ground on the strong ISM print, following recent softness tied to oil and geopolitics. Ten-year yields sit around 4.69-4.70 percent. Recent FOMC dissents for a hike plus resilient data have markets pricing elevated odds of tightening later in 2026, with Jackson Hole later this month in focus. A firmer dollar and higher-for-longer rates typically headwind crypto until risk appetite fully returns.
items.impact: Stronger dollar and hike pricing weigh on Bitcoin

items.title: Bessent: Hormuz Reopening Deal Possible Today or Tomorrow
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC the US and Iran could reach a deal as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz with full freedom of movement for commercial shipping. This follows Trump pausing planned strikes and calling talks Iran's last chance. Traders should care because the strait handles about 20 percent of global oil; a credible reopen would crush energy prices, ease inflation fears, and ignite risk-on flows into Bitcoin and equities.
items.impact: Sharp drop in oil likely to boost risk assets and crypto

items.title: US Nearly Exhausted Long-Range Precision Missiles in Iran War
items.summary: A Reuters report says the US has used virtually all its ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles during the five-month Iran conflict, with major drawdowns also in Patriots, THAADs, and Tomahawks. Military leaders have warned stockpiles now constrain options against other adversaries like China or Russia. This matters for traders because it signals real limits on US power projection, raises odds of a prolonged or messier Middle East war, and could force harder choices on Ukraine aid and Indo-Pacific deterrence.
items.impact: Heightens geopolitical risk premium and munitions supply concerns

items.title: Trump Pauses Iran Strikes for Last-Chance Diplomacy
items.summary: President Trump canceled imminent strikes after Gulf allies including Saudi Arabia urged restraint, declaring new talks Iran's final opportunity before potential decapitation strikes. Tehran has sent mixed signals, denying direct talks while negotiating a Hormuz route with Oman, and shipping remains disrupted. Crypto traders watch closely because unresolved energy chokepoint risk keeps oil volatile and risk appetite fragile until a real deal lands or collapses.
items.impact: Unresolved catalyst keeps oil and markets range-bound pending outcome

items.title: Ukraine Drone Strikes Kill Civilians in Russia as War Intensifies
items.summary: Ukrainian long-range drones hit Russian targets including a Wildberries warehouse and other sites, with reports of civilian deaths including children; Russia claimed intercepting over a thousand drones while launching its own large barrages. Zelensky also reshuffled key security posts, naming Rustem Umerov to head foreign intelligence. Ongoing high-tempo attrition and cross-border strikes sustain elevated global risk and munitions demand that compete with the Iran theater.
items.impact: Sustains elevated geopolitical risk and energy/commodity volatility

items.title: Ceuta Migrant Surge Aftermath Sparks Spain-Morocco Tensions
items.summary: After tens of thousands crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta late last week, most have returned but hundreds of minors remain stranded and at least dozens died. Ceuta's leader accused Morocco of encouraging or permitting the rush, triggering EU political friction and Spanish demands for solidarity. European migration flashpoints can quickly move politics, euros, and risk sentiment if they escalate into broader diplomatic or border crises.
items.impact: Raises European political risk and potential migration policy shifts

items.title: US Calls Chinese Coast Guard Patrols East of Taiwan Destabilizing
items.summary: China has intensified coast guard vessel patrols in waters east of Taiwan, prompting the US to label the activity deeply destabilizing and urge Beijing to stop its pressure campaign. Taiwan continues asserting South China Sea claims amid the broader pattern of gray-zone coercion. Any sharp rise in Taiwan Strait tensions would hit semiconductors, shipping, and global risk assets hard, making this a key secondary watch item alongside the Middle East.
items.impact: Elevates Indo-Pacific flashpoint risk for equities and tech supply chains
